outline.subject: The Mannheim Observatory was a tower observatory that operated in Mannheim before being relocated to Karlsruhe and eventually Heidelberg.

sections.title: Mannheim Observatory
sections.covers: This section provides an overview of the observatory's history, its relocation, and the current use of the original tower.

sections.title: Schwetzingen
sections.covers: This section describes the early astronomical activities of Christian Mayer and the establishment of an observatory at Schwetzingen Castle.

sections.title: The Palatinate Period
sections.covers: This section details the construction of the Mannheim Observatory and its development into a research facility under Christian Mayer.

sections.title: Christian Mayer’s Successors
sections.covers: This section outlines the challenges faced by the observatory's leadership and the damage sustained during the Napoleonic Era.

sections.title: The Baden Period
sections.covers: This section covers the decline of the observatory during the 19th century and the eventual decision to end the institute.

sections.title: Move to Karlsruhe
sections.covers: This section describes the appointment of Eduard Schönfeld, the move to Karlsruhe, and the eventual establishment of the observatory at Königstuhl.
